subject: Private VPC follow-up & network checklist \u2014 next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Liu <tom.liu@acmeanalytics.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-09T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Private VPC follow-up & network checklist — next steps

Hi Tom / Alicia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps: 

- Goal: Move production inference for Acme Analytics customer-facing features behind a Private VPC integration for data controls and egress isolation.
- Workloads: Mix of bursty real-time chat (low latency) and periodic batch embedding jobs.
- Preference: You mentioned leaning toward Private VPC (preferred) over Hosted API; we flagged Dedicated capacity as an intermediate option if you want reserved throughput but not a full VPC.

Network items we need to confirm to scope the Private VPC / AWS connection: 
1) Preferred connectivity method: AWS VPC Peering, AWS PrivateLink (Interface VPC Endpoint), or VPN? (each has tradeoffs — PrivateLink avoids cross-account route table changes but requires ENIs; peering has larger address-space considerations).
2) Cloud provider & account IDs (we only need the accounts participating in traffic).
3) CIDR ranges you want us to peering/route or to allowlist for management/egress.
4) Any egress NAT/Proxy constraints (do responses need to egress from your VPC or from our controlled egress IPs?).
5) Network owner/contact for engineering handoff (please loop them in).

I attached a short Private VPC checklist (redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf) that shows typical artifacts we exchange. 

Proposed next steps:
- Alicia / Tom to confirm preferred connectivity option and share the network contact (Raj or netops).
- Once we have account IDs and CIDRs, we’ll provide our required allowlist (egress IPs) and a basic peering/endpoint playbook.
- Redwood to draft an SOW and timeline after network confirmation (we generally see ~2–4 weeks for networking + testing).

If you prefer, we can set a 30-min tech sync with our infra engineer (Ethan) + your network lead to walk the checklist. 

Thanks — Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf (1 page PDF)

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@acmeanalytics.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-11-09T13:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC follow-up & network checklist — next steps

Thanks Sean — that summary looks right. We are leaning toward Private VPC (PrivateLink preferred if Redwood supports it) because we want minimal route table changes and tighter control on service endpoints.

Quick answers / notes: 
- Connectivity: Prefer PrivateLink (Interface endpoints) if you support it; otherwise VPC Peering is acceptable.
- Cloud: AWS (us-east-1) — I’ll confirm the specific account IDs.
- Network lead: looping in Raj (cc) who handles infra. Raj — can you share the account IDs and any CIDR constraints? Also flag any compliance needs (we have SOC2 + HIPAA scope).

We’d like to schedule the 30-min tech sync this week if possible. Our preference: Thu 11/11 9–10am PT.

Best,
Alicia
Director of Product | Acme Analytics

Hi Raj / Alicia —

Great, thanks for the details and the diagram. Confirming next items from Redwood: 

1) Attached is our current egress IPs file (redwood-egress-ips-2027.csv) — please allowlist these for health checks and any management callbacks. Note: for PrivateLink flows, we also publish endpoint DNS names; we’ll share the creation playbook during the tech sync.
2) We support both PrivateLink (preferred for most customers for the reasons you called out) and VPC Peering. For PrivateLink we’ll provide a step-by-step interface endpoint setup and the service name to use for your account.
3) Tech sync scheduled Thu 2027-11-11 09:00 PT — I’ll send an invite with dial-in and invite Ethan (infra engineer) to walk the network steps live.
4) SOW / timeline — based on the network handoff we’ll circulate a draft SOW and a two-week expedited timeline for networking + staging, or 3–4 weeks for a more conservative schedule.

Action items: 
- Raj: confirm VPC IDs and preferred endpoint VPC/subnet list during the tech sync.
